subject: biology-hl
topicLabel: C1.3 — Photosynthesis & C4.2 — Transfer of energy (Apr–May unit)

cards.back: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → glucose + 6O₂ — using light energy captured by chlorophyll. Respiration reversed.
Light energy → chemical energy stored in carbon compounds (glucose). The syllabus definition in one line.

cards.front: Where does the released oxygen come from?
cards.back: Photolysis of water at photosystem II — water is split for electrons, O₂ is the by-product. Confirmed with ¹⁸O-labelled water.
Red and blue strongly; green reflected → leaves look green. The action spectrum matches the absorption spectrum.
Rf = distance moved by pigment / distance moved by solvent. Each pigment has a characteristic Rf.
Dependent: thylakoid membranes (photosystems, photolysis, ATP + NADPH). Independent: stroma (Calvin cycle).

cards.front: What links the light-dependent reactions to the Calvin cycle?
cards.back: ATP and NADPH — the energy and hydrogen needed to reduce GP to triose phosphate in the stroma.
CO₂ combines with RuBP → glycerate 3-phosphate (GP), reduced to triose phosphate → glucose or RuBP regeneration.
Light intensity, CO₂ concentration and temperature — the graph plateaus when the next factor runs out; excess light can cause photoinhibition.
Rate graphs vs light intensity/CO₂: identify the limiting factor at each region of the curve and explain the plateau with the named next factor.
Autotroph capturing light energy through photosynthesis — the base of every food chain and pyramid of energy.

cards.front: Three ways energy is lost between trophic levels?
cards.back: Heat from respiration; uneaten/indigestible parts (egestion); excretion. Only ~10% passes to the next level.

cards.front: Why do food chains rarely exceed 4–5 trophic levels?
cards.back: After each ~10% transfer too little energy remains to sustain another population.

cards.front: Why are pyramids of energy always upright?
cards.back: Energy always decreases between levels (2nd law of thermodynamics) — unlike pyramids of numbers, which can invert.
Saprotroph: secretes enzymes and absorbs externally digested dead matter. Detritivore: ingests dead matter internally (earthworms, woodlice).

cards.front: Photosynthesis and respiration in the carbon cycle?
cards.back: Photosynthesis removes CO₂ from the atmosphere; respiration, combustion and decomposition add it back. Fossil fuels tip the balance.

cards.front: Which gas-releasing reactions belong to which process?
cards.back: CO₂: respiration + combustion. O₂: photosynthesis (photolysis). Hydrogen/CO₂ confusion is a common exam error.
Give the main steps in sequence without detail — e.g. photolysis → ATP/NADPH → Calvin cycle. Shorter than 'explain'.
Rate graphs vs light intensity/CO₂/temperature: name the limiting factor at each region and explain the plateau — standard question shape.
